scope: titles-v5 story matching: merging events whose articles match across (app/stories.py _nominate, _MemberEvidence, _member_support, merge rounds)
environment: macOS isolated copy of the titles-v4 rehearsal index (perf6: 89,575 items, 57,924 story memberships), schema 55; no network, no model calls
problem: Each article only compares with event anchors, so one event worded several ways became several events: 'Gemini breaks into three companies' was 8 events, AMD buying World Labs and Amazon pausing 21 Air 5 or more each. The anchor-only merge (story-merge-20261007.json) cannot join them because the anchors do not match.
design: After the per-item pass, each re-indexed article is compared with articles of other live events published within 72 h, the 60 sharing the most title trigrams first; candidates sharing under 30% of the shorter title's trigrams are skipped, and the length bound skips pairs that cannot reach 0.72.

A nominated pair of events merges when at least 2 of their article pairs score >= 0.72 (the later article compared with the earlier one), and the two anchors pass every hard rule of item matching (numbers, companies, filings, event types, stock-move trading day, 72 h).

The later event joins the earlier one and redirects there, as in the anchor merge. Merges repeat within one refresh on the merged memberships until none is left, so A~B and B~C join all three only when A's and C's anchors do not contradict each other.

A re-checked member that matches neither its anchor nor a former anchor stays when it matches at least 2 other members of its event; otherwise a former anchor of a merged event would leave and come back on every full reindex.

rejected_variants.variant: one matching article pair is enough
rejected_variants.result: 2 of 15 sampled pairs joined different events (funds each buying Amazon shares; vendors each joining Microsoft 365 Copilot); 1,139 merges instead of 638 in a simulation

rejected_variants.variant: at least 2 pairs, no chaining through a merged event
rejected_variants.result: first full reindex 584 merges, but a second reindex merged 192 more and moved items between 21 events: not stable

rejected_variants.variant: compare the 60 best candidates without the 30% trigram filter
rejected_variants.result: same pairs but 90 s instead of 38 s for the comparison; the filter misses 7 of 443 qualifying event pairs
dropped: copies of one headline already join the earliest copy's event during the per-item pass, and an identical copy in another event always brings a second matching pair

full_reindex.method: story_items.match_reason reset, refresh_derived() on a copy (starting from the titles-v4 result)

stability.method: second full reindex from the titles-v5 result

incremental_refresh_seconds.method: mark the N latest items dirty and refresh, same machine

reviewed_samples.reviewer: Claude, by reading the titles of the joined events; not owner labels

different_event_examples: MidFirst Bank / Argyle Capital Partners / Brightwater Advisory each buying Amazon shares (template titles)
unclear_examples: Meta-linked data centre junk bonds / CleanSpark bonds for Meta-linked AI infrastructure

large_merges: Gemini breaking into three companies: 144 articles from 5+ events
storyline_merges: Trump attacking the Anthropic CEO's call joined the call itself (129 articles)

query_plans: the window query searches idx_items_pub; membership queries search idx_story_items_story
limits: No owner-labelled story pairs exist yet; precision is a reading of sampled titles.
Template titles (13F fund purchases, quote pages, generic stock-move pieces) match one another and still merge.
Follow-ups of one storyline within 72 h can join one event when their anchors do not contradict each other.
The cutover starts from titles-v2 memberships, not titles-v4; its reindex time was measured for titles-v4 only (193-213 s) and is expected near +40 s.
tests: tests/test_story_merge.py: events whose articles match across merge on the second matching pair (one is not enough), and a full reindex keeps them; anchors that contradict each other keep their events apart; an event joins through a third once the first merge is made (no direct pair between them); an article matching only one other article does not stay; earlier anchor-merge and no-chain tests unchanged
10 of 11 mutations of the new rules fail a test; the survivor reverses the comparison direction (earlier compared with later), an equally deterministic convention
